## EMST role: Geospatial and remote sensing analyst (state variant, journey level; P1)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.35, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa:R04-geospatial-remote-sensing-analyst/state:516L`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Analyze remotely sensed data to map and monitor environmental conditions — journey L2 *(distinguishing)*
- Conduct spatial analysis and modelling of environmental data — journey L2
- Protect sensitive ecological, cultural and personal information in data products — journey L2
- Conduct reproducible, auditable environmental analysis, including AI-assisted code — journey L2
- Evaluate model fitness-for-purpose and validate against independent evidence — journey L2 *(distinguishing)*
- Quantify and communicate uncertainty for environmental decisions — journey L2
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L2
- Ground-truth remote-sensed, modelled and AI-generated outputs in the field — journey L1
- Design maps and visualizations that communicate environmental data and uncertainty — journey L2
- Build and validate automated detection and classification models for environmental observations — journey L2
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1
- Steward and publish environmental data for reuse — journey L2
- Design and manage environmental databases — journey L2

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Interpret satellite and aerial imagery to detect changes in vegetation, soil or water condition across a management area between two dates. — 11.0% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Classify preprocessed multispectral imagery into land-cover types using training data whose collection method and date are documented. — 10.9% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Preprocess imagery for analysis by correcting geometry, radiometry and cloud or shadow contamination, documenting each step and its parameters. — 7.3% *(needed at entry)*
- Assess the accuracy of a remotely sensed map against independent field reference data, reporting error by class and condition. — 7.3% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Run spatial queries and overlays for an environmental assessment, checking that all layers share a coordinate reference system and compatible scales. — 7.3% *(needed at entry)*
- Analyze terrain, habitat connectivity or resource distribution for a planning question, stating the data, projection and accuracy limits that bound the answer. — 7.3% *(needed at entry)*
- Build a predictive spatial model for a conservation planning question, documenting its inputs, assumptions and validation against independent locations. — 7.3%
- Design a map for a stated audience and decision, choosing scale, extent, symbology and colour that the audience reads correctly. — 7.3% *(needed at entry)*
- Check whether a map product shares training data with the reference used to validate it, choosing an independent reference when it does. — 3.6% *(critical)*
- Maintain spatial layers of land use, vegetation and infrastructure with topology rules, attribute standards and update dates recorded. — 3.6% *(needed at entry)*
- Depict the uncertainty of a mapped or charted estimate with an encoding that intended users read correctly in a comprehension check. — 3.6%
- Produce maps for reports, briefings and field crews at the scale, extent and legibility each use requires. — 3.6% *(needed at entry)*

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* 1 not shown until the issuer is verified

## EMST role: Hydrologist (state variant, journey level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:relatedMatch`, confidence 0.35, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-wa:R17-hydrologist/state:516L`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Plan water supply and allocation under hydrologic uncertainty — journey L2 *(distinguishing)*
- Characterize groundwater systems and protect drinking water sources — journey L2
- Build, calibrate and validate predictive and simulation models of environmental systems — journey L2
- Quantify and communicate uncertainty for environmental decisions — journey L2
- Assess stream channel form and function in the field — journey L2
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — journey L2
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — journey L2
- Develop pollutant load allocations and watershed restoration plans for impaired waters — journey L2
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1
- Evaluate model fitness-for-purpose and validate against independent evidence — journey L2
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1
- Deploy, maintain and verify field sensor networks — journey L2
- Analyze and interpret climate observations and projections for management decisions — journey L2

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Prepare a drought contingency plan with triggers, stages and response actions tied to supply indicators — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Run an aquifer test on a supply well or wellfield to estimate transmissivity and storage from drawdown and recovery data — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Delineate a wellhead or source-water protection area from hydrogeologic data and time-of-travel criteria — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Simulate ecosystem response to alternative land-use and climate scenarios, documenting scenario assumptions and the sensitivity of results to each. — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Forecast water demand and supply under drought and climate scenarios for a utility or basin plan, stating assumptions and uncertainty — 4.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Compare conjunctive-use, reuse and storage options by yield, cost and reliability for an integrated resource plan — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Review a well construction or injection well application against construction and protection standards before approval — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Build a predictive model of fire risk, pest outbreak or water availability, validating it on years or areas withheld from fitting. — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Forecast resource management needs from a validated predictive model, stating the horizon and interval for each estimate. — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Survey channel cross-sections, longitudinal profile and substrate at a reach following the geomorphic assessment protocol — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Identify bankfull indicators and channel evolution stage at a reach from field evidence — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
